newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia wants pilot brought home for drug trial.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia wants pilot brought home for drug trial.

text.p: Indonesia wants the pilot from national airline Garuda Indonesia who has been charged in the Netherlands with narcotics smuggling to face trial at home, the evening daily Suara Pembaruan reported on Wednesday.
The pilot was arrested at Amsterdam's Schipol airport on Sunday with 8,000 pills of the designer drug ecstasy strapped to his body.
Indonesian Attorney General Singgih said punishments for those involved in ecstasy smuggling in the Netherlands were too light and were much heavier in Indonesia.
"Although we do not have an extradition treaty with Holland, maybe Interpol could hand over the pilot to us," he was quoted as saying.
The official news agency Antara quoted Singgih as saying on Wednesday that his office would check reports that the pilot had been badly treated in the Netherlands.

Indonesian embassy staff in The Hague criticised Dutch police earlier this week for not allowing them to see the pilot, arrested as he was about to board a Garuda flight bound for Indonesia's holiday island of Bali.

The Kompas daily reported on Wednesday that Indonesian customs have seized 202,000 ecstasy pills at Jakarta's main Sukarno-Hatta International airport since April. Most of the drugs were carried by Indonesians and foreigners flying from Amsterdam, it said.
Indonesia is preparing a law to ban trade in, and use of, ecstasy, which has gained popularity in recent years.
